summary: A contents search keeps, for each file it lists, the line its row shows: `ContentHit { line, text }` in `Finder::content_hits` (src/finder/mod.rs), filled by `content_search`, which now returns `(rows, lines, stats)`, and cleared or replaced in the three places `results` is written. The Text and Code arms of `preview_body` (src/finder/preview.rs) go through one `text_preview`. For a result whose line is past the file's first lines it draws the text in two blocks inside `MatchScroll`: a scroll area built from the parts of the kit's scrollbar wrapper (ScrollBounce, the axis lock, the kit's scrollbar) around a ScrollHandle kept in element state under the file's path ID, which is asked to put the second block, starting up to two lines above the match, at the top, once per file and line. A new handle has no bounds from a frame before and would overshoot, so the first frame draws the area empty and asks for the next one. A match in the first lines is only marked. One past the 64 KB a preview reads opens the preview at its end, where the truncated note names the line. The mark is made by `with_mark` (the name-match highlight behind the line, the plain text colour in place of the grammar's) and only while the preview's line starts with the text the search found (`hit_range`). Every other text or code preview keeps the kit's wrapper and is pixel-identical. Markdown is untouched.
changelog: The preview of a contents search result opens at the matching line. A text or code preview used to show such a file from its first line, in the Preview Pane, the gallery, and Quick Look, and you had to find the line the list names by eye. It now opens at that line, with up to two lines before it in view and the rest of the file a scroll away. The line is highlighted and drawn in the plain text color, so that it reads on the highlight. When the match is further into a file than the first 64 KB a preview reads, the preview opens at its end, where "preview truncated" says which line the match is on. A file that has changed since the search, so that the line reads differently, opens at its top with nothing highlighted. Markdown previews stay rendered and open at the top.
behaviour_changes: In the results of a contents search, a text or code preview opens at the matching line its row shows instead of at the file's first line: in the Preview Pane, the gallery, Quick Look's window, and Quick Look's dialog in --term mode. Up to two lines before the match stay in view (fewer when they add up to more than 160 bytes, so that long lines can't wrap the match out of a small preview), and the rest of the file is a scroll away in both directions. Seen in pictures for plain text, code, CSV, JSON, TOML, a shell script, a .nu script, Windows line ends, a byte order mark, tabs, letters of several bytes and emoji, a 1,500-character line, a line longer than the 512 bytes the search keeps, and a last line with no line break.

The line is highlighted from its first character, indentation included, to the end of its text, with the colour that marks matches in names, and drawn in the plain text colour: on that one line the syntax colours are dropped, bold and italic stay. A long line is highlighted as a whole, however far it wraps.

A match on one of the file's first three lines is highlighted and the preview is not scrolled, unless the lines above it are too long to keep (over 160 bytes), when it is scrolled past them. From line 4 on the preview is scrolled, if only by a line.
A match past the first 64 KB: the preview opens at its end, and the note reads "… (preview truncated; the match on line N is further down)" instead of "… (preview truncated)".

The preview goes to the line once per file and line: when the file comes on screen, when the search finds another line in the same file, when the file is shown again after another one, and after Refresh, which forgets every preview (my probe saw the scrolled preview back at the match). By the same rule, read from the code and not tried, it goes there again whenever the preview was not drawn for a frame: another tab shown and back, the preview pane closed and opened. It stays where it is being read when the search only runs again without that (the retry while indexing, run_search from a setting) and when the text size changes. The implementer's report listed Refresh among the things that leave it in place; that is wrong, and neither the commit message nor the manual says so.

If the preview's line no longer starts with what the row shows (the file changed after the search, or the preview kept from before is older than the search), the preview opens at its top with nothing highlighted.
Markdown previews are unchanged: rendered, at the top, nothing highlighted.

A preview that opens at a line draws its area empty for one frame, asks for the next frame itself, and has the text in place in that one. Followed frame by frame in the pane and in Quick Look's window without the harness's forced frames; no further frames are asked for once the text is drawn.

At the match, the lines above it start right at the top edge of the preview area, without the 12 points of padding, as in any scrolled preview. Scrolled back to its top or on to its end, such a preview has the same padding as the others (measured: first line 12 points below the edge, last line 12 above, in both kinds of area).

Previews outside a contents search are unchanged: pixel-identical in the implementer's 15 pictures and in 18 of my own from the trunk's source and from the change (text, code, JSON, TOML, shell, Markdown, a truncated log, an empty file, a one-line file, a CR-only file; pane light and dark, gallery, column card, Quick Look). Only the status bar's milliseconds differ.

A file with old Mac line ends (carriage returns only) is one line to the search. Its preview, which was an empty area before and still is outside a search (see Found, not fixed), shows its first line and a block of highlight as a result.
Not visible: the note under a truncated preview has the element ID `preview-note` and an accessibility label that is its text.
docs/manual.md: the Contents row of the scope bar table, and the Markdown and "Code and other text" rows of the preview table.
left_out: Brief step 4 (read a 64 KB window around a far match) and step 5 ("N matching lines" in the caption): cut by the verifier, not done.
Later matches in the same file are not marked: the engine is asked for one line a file, the one the row shows.
Only the whole line is marked, not the words that matched in it. content-match-highlight will have the ranges.

Markdown results stay rendered, open at the top and have nothing marked (the brief's first option); the manual says so. For someone who searches notes kept in Markdown this is the common case, so drawing the source while the file is a result may be worth a brief of its own.

A match on the line a truncated preview stops reading in (the one across byte 65,536), when less of that line was read than the search kept of it: not marked, no note, the preview opens at its top (picture -review-quicklook-cut-line.png). It fails towards the old behaviour and needs the first match of a file to be exactly there. A way in: let `hit_range` accept the cut line when the row's text starts with what was read of it.

No test sees the highlight drawn. With the `with_mark` call taken out of `text_preview` every test passes: `preview_match_for_test` finds the line the same way the drawing does but doesn't look at what is drawn, and the harness can't see text runs. `with_mark` itself has a unit test, and the pictures show the mark.
The split text is not cached: per frame, while a result's preview shows, one scan for the line, one pass over the spans for the mark, one for the split, and two string copies, all bounded by 64 KB.
README.md states nothing that changed. The Search Syntax dialog is not affected. CHANGELOG.md is not edited, as the guide says; the entry is in the commit message.

Nothing was built or run on macOS or Windows. The change has no platform-specific code; the kit's bounce, which the area is wrapped in as the kit's own wrapper is, is on only on macOS, and the tests run with reduced motion.
tests: tests/basics.rs: a_preview_opens_at_the_line_a_contents_search_found (pane: text, code, a match in the first lines, a far match, a search run again, a file gone back to, the search ended)
tests/basics.rs: quick_look_opens_at_the_line_a_contents_search_found (Quick Look's window; bigger text keeps the place; a far match)
tests/basics.rs: a_preview_that_opens_at_a_line_shows_its_text_in_the_next_frame (added in review: Quick Look's window, frame by frame as the platform delivers them)
review_fixes: New test a_preview_that_opens_at_a_line_shows_its_text_in_the_next_frame (tests/basics.rs). The area is drawn empty in its first frame and `MatchScroll` asks for the next with window.request_animation_frame(), and no test covered that: the harness forces a frame after every step, so with the request taken out all eleven tests passed, while in Quick Look's window, where nothing else asks for a frame, the preview stayed empty until the browser drew again (my probe). The test clicks a result without the harness's frame, sees the area empty in Quick Look's window, delivers that window's next frame the way the platform does (window.simulate_next_frame) and expects the text at the match. It fails with the request removed.
The five new unit tests in src/finder/preview.rs sat at the end of the file, where the guide asks lanes not to add. They now stand before previews_by_kind, unchanged.
Commit message: one sentence added on the area asking for its second frame itself and why Quick Look's window needs it.

Rebased onto 65da066 and 06d84e9, which had landed before the review began, and then onto 26ab60c (sorted-search-results), which landed during it and changed the search code in src/finder/mod.rs: no conflict, `SearchStats` has `sort_chooses` in both of the places this change also touches, and `results` is still written in the same three places. check.sh ran on the result each time.
notes:
Checked. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the trunk commit 7228253: 574 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures (556 on the same change one trunk commit earlier). `cargo check --lib -p fffinder`, the library as it ships without test-support, has no warnings. The six UI tests of this change also passed with 14 different SEEDs, one trunk commit before the last rebase.

Tests fail without the change. With the src diff reverse-applied the --term test fails at the missing preview-match, and tests/basics.rs doesn't compile (preview_match_for_test), so I took the behaviour out a piece at a time behind a switch, 18 ways, and ran the new tests under each. Each of these made at least one fail: no line reaching the preview; lines not kept after the search ended (the last part of the pane test); the answer's lines not installed; none collected; the plain note for a far match; a far match left at the top; the guard off (the changed-file test and its unit test); lines counted from 0; no lines of context; the 160-byte rule off; grammar colours kept; the split's spans off by one; the jump asked for in the first frame (pane, gallery and --term fail, as the implementer says: the block lands at the window's top); the jump on every frame; the jump only once however the line changes; no jump. Two passed everything: no request for the second frame, which the new test now catches, and the mark not drawn, which is in left_out.

Probes and pictures, not kept in the repository. (1) Frames, following the platform's order with no forced refresh: after a click on a result whose preview is already read, the pane and Quick Look's window each draw once with the area empty; the next-frame callbacks run; the text is drawn at the match; no callback is left. (2) Extents: scrolled to its top and to its end, the area built here puts the first and last line exactly where the kit's wrapper does (12 points from the edge). A match on the file's last line opens with that line at the bottom; a short file isn't scrolled. (3) The --term dialog with motion on: while it slides in the block moves with it and comes to rest exactly where it is with reduced motion (153 px in both), so the implementer's worry that the slide could put the jump off did not show. (4) Refresh and theme: see behaviour_changes and Found, not fixed. (5) 15 hard files of my own (-review-mkdemo.py, -review-shots.sh, and the sheets -review-sheet-hard-1/2.png), the narrow pane at 180 points, 24-point text in the gallery and Quick Look, dark theme.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt a user, and what the code says.
(1) A result's preview stays empty, or flickers without end. The area is empty only in the frame its state is made in (`new` is set inside use_keyed_state's init), that frame asks for the next, and the state lives while the preview is drawn in consecutive frames. The probes above show the second frame arriving by the platform's own path in the pane and in Quick Look's window, and no frame asked for after it. What is left is one frame of the preview's background without text, between the spinner or the previous file's text and this file's; I could not look at that on a real display.
(2) The preview jumps away from where it is being read. The jump is asked for when the state is new or `at` differs from the line, nothing else. A search that runs again installs the same line (test; the jump-every-frame mutant fails it). Bigger text keeps the element and its state (test). The answer replaces `results` and `content_hits` together, so there is no frame without the line in between. It does go to the match again after Refresh, a theme change, or another tab, where any preview goes back to its top.
(3) A mark, or the view, on the wrong line. fff-search hands on the line without its terminators, cut to 512 bytes at a character boundary, decoded lossily, leading space trimmed (grep/sink.rs, grep.rs, fuzzy_grep.rs, regex.rs; the same in every mode), and counts lines by line feeds, as `line_range` does. `hit_range` marks a line only if the preview's line starts with that text, so a stale preview or a changed file gets no mark instead of a wrong one. `content_hit` is not gated on the search being a contents search; instead the map is emptied or replaced in every place `results` is (set_query's empty branch, drop_stale_results, the answer), and navigating ends the search through set_query. A rename of a result leaves its row without a line and its preview without a mark, which agree. Split view, tabs and --pick windows are each a Finder view of their own with its own lines and its own element state; I read that and did not try it.

Doubts that remain.
1. Only Linux was built and run.
2. The empty first frame on a real display (above). If it shows, one handle per surface that lives across files would have bounds from the frame before and could jump at once, at the price of the stale-bounds cases this design avoids.
3. Two things are the implementer's calls beyond the brief, both in the manual and the changelog: the marked line loses its grammar colours (a gray comment on the mark in the dark theme measured 1.5 to 1; `color: None` in with_mark and its unit test to go back), and a far match opens the preview at its end, where the note is, not at its top.
4. In a file whose match is on line 4 the preview is scrolled by one line and hides line 1, where not scrolling would show both. The rule is simple (two lines above the match at the top) and I left it.

For briefs still to come.
- preview-page-keys: a text or code preview now scrolls in one of two areas. Most keep the kit's wrapper (`.overflow_y_scrollbar().id(("text-preview" | "code-preview", path_id))`, its handle private to the kit). A contents search result that opens at a line scrolls in `MatchScroll`, whose ScrollHandle is in `MatchScrollState`, kept with window.use_keyed_state under the same ID in `MatchScroll::render`. Keys that scroll a text preview have to reach both. Element path of the second: .., "fffinder::finder::preview::MatchScroll", ("text-preview", id), (id, "bounce"), (id, "area"), then "preview-text", "preview-match" and "preview-note".
- table-preview-scroll: the table and font arms are untouched. `MatchScroll` is a worked example of a scroll area with a handle of one's own inside the kit's bounce and with its scrollbar; mind that a new handle asked to go to an item in its first frame overshoots by the area's distance from the window's top (div.rs: scroll_to_active_item runs before clamp_scroll_position stores the frame's bounds).
- stale-previews-and-cancel: (a) `preview_match_for_test` reads `self.previews.get(path)` and matches `Preview::Text | Preview::Code`; follow your new value type there. (b) A preview older than the search opens at its top with nothing marked, by `hit_range`; once you read a changed file again the mark returns by itself. a_preview_marks_no_line_when_the_file_changed_after_the_search rewrites log.txt after the search has answered and before the file is first previewed, so it does not depend on a stale cache and should hold. (c) A preview replaced in place keeps its `MatchScroll` state and doesn't jump unless the line changes; a spinner frame in between ends the state, and the preview goes to the match again, as after Refresh today. (d) The theme bug under Found, not fixed is in the code you restructure.
- content-match-highlight: content_search's loop is now `let (line, text) = (hit.line, hit.text.trim().to_string()); rows.push(Row::new(entry, Vec::new(), Some(format!("{line}: {text}")))); lines.insert(hit.path, ContentHit { line, text });`. `ContentHit.text` has to stay the start of the file's line (what the engine hands on, trimmed): `hit_range` compares it with `starts_with` against the preview's line after trim_start. If the row is to show a snippet that starts near the match, build that for the row and leave `ContentHit.text` alone, or every mark and jump disappears. With your ranges the preview could mark the words instead of the line: `with_mark(spans, &range, color)` takes any byte range of the preview's text (your ranges are in the trimmed line, so add the line's leading space).
- regex-content-search: `content_search` returns `(rows, lines, stats)`; fill `lines` in your mode too, and return an empty map for an invalid pattern. A match over several lines has its first line as the line's text (fff-search regex.rs), which is what the guard needs.
- live-search-results: a quiet rerun has to replace `content_hits` with `results`, as run_search's answer does. Finding the same line leaves a preview where it is being read; another line takes it there. When the previewed file itself changed, the kept preview no longer matches the row and loses its mark until it is read again.
- search-start-no-flash, back-forward-restore-search, smart-folder-save-and-leaks, restore-session-tabs: `content_hits` is written beside `results` in set_query's empty branch, drop_stale_results and run_search's answer; keep the pairs together. If rows are ever put back without searching, put their lines back too, or the previews open at the top.
- preview-card-height: MATCH_CONTEXT_BYTES (160) was chosen so that the lines kept above a match can't wrap it out of the 240-point card at the pane's least width (180; picture -review-sheet-narrow-pane.png); a taller card only helps. The pane tests measure from preview-pane's top and turn the wheel 100 points below it; none depends on the 240.
- quick-look-empty-state, quick-look-window-mixup: a_preview_that_opens_at_a_line_shows_its_text_in_the_next_frame expects Quick Look's window to have drawn exactly once after a click in the browser (through the observer in QuickLookWindow::new) and to draw the text when its own next frame is delivered. If the window comes to follow the browser another way and draws twice at the click, its first assertion ("the first frame has no text yet") is the one to adjust; the second is the point.
- view-switch-keeps-selection: a result kept selected across a view switch is drawn on another surface, with a new state, so its preview goes to the match again.
- image-preview-details, thumbnail-memory: no arm in common; expect at most a textual conflict near `preview_body`, whose Text and Code arms now call `text_preview`.
- sorted-search-results is under this commit on the trunk: sorting a contents search's rows reorders them and leaves `content_hits`, which is by path, alone.

Found, not fixed (all on the trunk before this change).
- With the Preview Pane open, Toggle Light/Dark leaves the pane's preview as a spinner until another item is selected: toggle_appearance, set_appearance, adopt_settings and the system-appearance observer forget every preview, and nothing reads the selected item's again. The gallery asks on every frame and recovers. My probe: after ToggleAppearance, has_preview_for_test is false and no preview-text is drawn, in a folder and in a search. Worth a brief, or a line in stale-previews-and-cancel.
- A text file with carriage returns only (old Mac line ends) previews as an empty area: nothing is drawn for a line with a bare carriage return inside it (picture -review-sheet-cr-only.png, left; identical before and after this change).
- Text in Latin-1 with many accented letters has no text preview: read_text takes 16 replacement characters for a binary file. A contents search lists such a file with its line all the same.
